replies.question: How does Brad ship with AI agents?
replies.text:
Brad ships with AI agents mainly through VINDecoded, a side project where the work runs on a human-approved system. Brad runs VINDecoded, a profitable vehicle-research product on Android, iOS and the web, where AI agents write most of the code and Brad reviews and approves the work. The system around the agents includes docs every agent reads before it starts, one isolated checkout per agent, tests the coding agent can't rewrite, a second agent that reviews its work, a gate and a kill switch on every new feature, and one audited door to production.

Some of the specific rules are enforced rather than just written. The agent writes tests first and watches them fail for the right reason. Then a small script locks them by recording each file's hash. When the code is done, a second agent reviews it with fresh context and only read tools, so it can't quietly fix what it finds.

Releases are kept separate from merging. Merging to master deploys nothing. A release happens only when Brad asks for one. Most new features reach production turned off, so merging and deploying code doesn't change what customers see.

The scale of this work is also recorded. The case study's counts, measured on 10/28: 1,235 merged PRs from June 13 to Oct 28, 2026, 83% of them from agent branches.
